stem: A insurer's on-premises batch servers upload files to Cloud Storage and query BigQuery over HA VPN tunnels, never over the internet. The security team also runs VPC Service Controls around the data projects and wants the servers to be unable to reach any Google API that VPC Service Controls cannot protect. Which design meets this?

choices.text: Give each on-premises server a public route to Google APIs, then add VPC Service Controls ingress rules that deny any API request arriving from outside the perimeter
Resolve all Google API names on premises to the private.googleapis.com addresses, and advertise that range through the Cloud Router so every Google API stays reachable over the tunnels
Enable Private Google Access on the VPC subnets that terminate the tunnels, because that setting also covers requests that originate in the on-premises network
Resolve all Google API names on premises to the restricted.googleapis.com addresses, and advertise that range from the Cloud Router

stem: After a migration, on-premises clients that use Private Google Access for on-premises hosts show intermittent failures: some Cloud Storage calls succeed and others time out. Investigation shows the on-premises DNS zone for googleapis.com holds an A record for restricted.googleapis.com, but the CNAME and a manually added A record for storage.googleapis.com use addresses from the private.googleapis.com range. Routes and tunnels are healthy. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Point every record in the zone at one virtual IP range, either restricted or private, and do not mix addresses from both
Move the manual storage.googleapis.com record to a public DNS zone so that the resolver chooses the nearest address
Raise the TTL on the googleapis.com records so that clients cache one answer and always use the same address
Add a second Cloud Router in another region so that both address ranges are advertised over separate tunnels

stem: A media firm is allowed to use only Google APIs that VPC Service Controls supports in its regulated analytics environment, but its marketing environment, connected to the same data center, must also call Google Maps Platform APIs from on premises. Which approach respects both rules with the least duplication?

choices.text: Use public Google API addresses for marketing and the restricted range for analytics, since the private range excludes Maps APIs
Use restricted.googleapis.com for all on-premises resolvers, since the stricter range also reaches the Google Maps Platform APIs
Use the restricted range for regulated resolvers and the private range for marketing resolvers, each in its own DNS scope
Use private.googleapis.com for all on-premises resolvers and rely on a VPC Service Controls perimeter to block unsupported services

stem: To remove an exfiltration path, a network engineer deleted the default 0.0.0.0/0 route from a VPC network that hosts private VMs with no external IP addresses. Since then, those VMs can no longer call Google APIs, even though DNS already maps googleapis.com names to the restricted.googleapis.com addresses. What is the minimal change that keeps the internet closed while restoring API access?

choices.text: Create a Cloud NAT gateway for the subnets so that the VMs can reach Google APIs through translated source addresses
Add a custom static route for the restricted.googleapis.com range whose next hop is the default internet gateway
Re-create the 0.0.0.0/0 route and add an egress deny firewall rule for everything except Google API names
Add a VPC Network Peering connection to the Google services network so that API requests travel as internal traffic

stem: A bank wants each business unit's workloads and its on-premises data center to reach Cloud Storage and BigQuery using internal IP addresses that the bank allocates itself, with a separate endpoint per unit so network teams can steer, monitor and prove that traffic stays inside Google Cloud. Which feature fits best?

choices.text: Direct peering with Google, which exposes Cloud Storage and BigQuery on the bank's own address space
Private Google Access enabled on the subnets, because it assigns a dedicated internal address from the bank's range per business unit
A Cloud NAT gateway per business unit, which gives each unit its own translated address for outbound calls to Google APIs
Private Service Connect endpoints for Google APIs, using the vpc-sc API bundle for regulated units, with DNS names that map to each endpoint

stem: An engineer creates a Private Service Connect endpoint named logs1 for Google APIs with the all-apis bundle and expects VMs to call storage-logs1.p.googleapis.com privately. A packet capture shows the traffic going to public Google addresses. The endpoint's forwarding rule is healthy and the VMs have no external IP addresses. What most likely explains this?

choices.text: Endpoints can only be reached from the same region as the forwarding rule, and the VMs run in another region
Private Service Connect for Google APIs needs a peering connection to the Google services network before DNS names work
The VMs resolve the name where no private zone has it, so public DNS wildcard answers return public addresses
The all-apis bundle sends traffic to public front ends unless subnets also have Private Google Access on

stem: A SaaS vendor publishes a managed service behind a Private Service Connect service attachment that explicitly accepts connections only from approved customer projects. A new customer creates an endpoint in its VPC network that targets the attachment, but the connection stays in the Pending state indefinitely. What should the vendor check first?

choices.text: Whether the customer's endpoint uses the same Service Directory namespace as the vendor's published service
Whether the customer's project is on the accept list and whether connection capacity remains
Whether a VPC Network Peering connection exists between the two VPC networks
Whether the customer's subnet range overlaps with the vendor's NAT subnet and must be renumbered

stem: A healthcare company publishes records through a regional managed service that it accesses via Private Service Connect. The security team wants to terminate TLS on its own certificate and domain in front of the service, apply Cloud Armor and centralised logging to the traffic, and fail over between two regions under its own control. Which Private Service Connect type should it use?

choices.text: Private Service Connect backends, using network endpoint groups behind an internal or external Application Load Balancer
Private Service Connect interfaces, because they let the consumer terminate certificates for the producer's service
Private services access, because its allocated range provides load balancer features for managed services
Private Service Connect endpoints, because a forwarding rule gives the same control over certificates and fail over

stem: A retailer connects its data center to Google Cloud with Dedicated Interconnect. A new policy says all traffic between on-premises networks and VPC networks must be encrypted at the network layer from end to end, not only on the physical link. Which design meets this?

choices.text: HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect, with IPsec tunnels established over the VLAN attachments
MACsec on the Interconnect circuit alone, since it encrypts traffic between the two networks
A second Dedicated Interconnect connection in another metro, since redundant circuits encrypt each path
TLS on the application load balancers, since it encrypts all packets in the VPC network at layer 3

stem: A network architect is reviewing MACsec for Cloud Interconnect for a Dedicated Interconnect link and a Partner Interconnect link. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: MACsec encrypts traffic all the way to the VM in the VPC network, inside Google's network too
On Partner Interconnect, the customer should work with the service provider so traffic is encrypted through the provider's network
Enabling MACsec makes IPsec and TLS redundant, so Google recommends dropping them
MACsec establishes IPsec tunnels that terminate on a Cloud Router in the VPC network
MACsec encrypts traffic between the on-premises router and Google's edge router

stem: On-premises hosts in the Frankfurt region reach Google APIs through the restricted VIP over two VLAN attachments that connect to a VPC network. Requests leave the data center, but responses never arrive. The routes to the on-premises networks learned in the VPC network have next hops on a Cloud VPN tunnel and a VLAN attachment, both in a different region than the one the requests entered. What is the likely cause?

choices.text: The Cloud Router advertises the restricted range with a higher MED, so Google drops the requests
The restricted range is only reachable from on-premises IPv6 hosts, which Frankfurt does not use
VPC firewall rules have an implied deny egress rule that blocks all replies to the on-premises network
The next hop toward on-premises is in another region than the request origin, so responses cannot return

stem: A company has private build VMs in a subnet and sensitive data-processing VMs in another, and none of the VMs has an external IP address. Only the build VMs may download packages from the internet, and the security team wants no other VM to be able to initiate internet connections. What is the best design?

choices.text: Place a Cloud Router in the sensitive subnet, because it filters outbound connections by the source VM
Configure a Cloud NAT gateway that serves all subnets in the region, then add a firewall rule to block the sensitive VMs from using it
Configure a Cloud NAT gateway serving only the build subnet, and give the sensitive subnet no NAT and no external IPs
Give the build VMs external IP addresses, because Cloud NAT cannot be limited to a subset of a VPC network

stem: A partner reports suspicious scanning from one of the retailer's shared Cloud NAT external IP addresses. Hundreds of private VMs use that gateway, and the security team must work out which VM made the connections, using the gateway's records. What should have been configured on the gateway?

choices.text: Cloud NAT logging of translations, recording each connection with its internal VM and external address
A larger set of external IP addresses, because each VM then receives its own address that identifies it uniquely
Cloud NAT logging for errors only, because dropped packets reveal every VM that opened a connection
VPC flow logs only on the Cloud Router, because the router records the NAT translations

stem: A consortium member's VPC network is peered with a partner's VPC network so a reporting application can reach one subnet, subnet-a. A second subnet, subnet-b, in the same VPC network holds regulated data and must stay unreachable from the partner. The partner's address ranges are known. What is the right control?

choices.text: A route filter on the peering connection that excludes subnet-b from the routes exchanged
Network tags on the partner's VMs matching tags in the member's ingress rules so only tagged VMs reach subnet-a
Firewall rules created by the partner's administrators, because peered networks apply each other's firewall rules to incoming traffic
Ingress rules in the member's own network allowing the partner ranges only to subnet-a targets, with implied deny for subnet-b

stem: A security architect is reviewing how a Cloud NAT gateway for Public NAT behaves before approving it for private workloads. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Internet hosts can open new connections to a private VM through the gateway's external address once a source port is allocated
Each external address of the gateway is bound to one VM, so a remote party can tell from the address which VM connected
The gateway is a distributed, software-defined service configured on a Cloud Router, with no proxy VMs in the traffic path
Cloud NAT must be configured before VMs can reach Google APIs through the restricted.googleapis.com virtual IP range
The gateway translates only the subnets or subnet ranges selected for it, so VMs in other subnets of the region get no NAT from it

stem: A platform team runs a Shared VPC with one host project and many service projects. The security team wants to ensure that no team can attach its project to a host project outside the approved one, and that each team can place VMs and load balancers only in the shared subnets assigned to it. Which controls should be used?

choices.text: One organization-wide Compute Network User grant to all developers, with firewall rules limiting each team
Org policy constraints on allowed host projects and usable subnets, plus subnet-level Compute Network User grants
VPC Network Peering between each service project's own VPC network and the host project's network instead of Shared VPC
Giving each service project administrator the Shared VPC Admin role, so they can manage their own subnet assignments

stem: A team connects workloads to a managed Cloud SQL instance. It currently uses private services access, which allocates an IP range and peers with the Google-managed producer network. The security team now wants a design where the instance appears at an IP address chosen from the consumer subnet, each consumer project has its own connection, and on-premises clients reach the instance over a hybrid link without extra custom route export. What should the team use?

choices.text: Cloud NAT, which translates the instance's address for the on-premises clients
Private Service Connect for Cloud SQL, with an endpoint in a consumer subnet
A Private Google Access setting on the subnet, which lets Cloud SQL be reached by internal IP
Another private services access range, with custom routes exported on the peering to on premises

stem: A security engineer lists requirements for letting on-premises hosts reach Google APIs privately over Cloud VPN or VLAN attachments with Private Google Access for on-premises hosts. Which TWO items are required? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A Cloud NAT gateway in the VPC network that translates the on-premises hosts' addresses
A Compute Engine VM in every subnet that acts as a forwarding proxy for API calls
An external IP address on every on-premises host that calls the API, so Google can verify the source of requests
Routes for the chosen address range in both the on-premises network and the VPC network, so traffic enters the tunnel or attachment
On-premises DNS records resolving API names to the private.googleapis.com or restricted.googleapis.com addresses

stem: A car insurer lets customers upload photos of driver's licences and claim forms to Cloud Storage. Before sending images to a third-party damage-assessment team, the insurer must obscure names, licence numbers and addresses printed in the images, and hide any visible licence plates. Which approach meets this?

choices.text: Use character masking transformations on the image files, replacing characters in the picture with asterisks
Run a discovery scan configuration, which blurs sensitive areas in images in the bucket after profiling
Use image redaction with infoTypes for text and licence plate objects, and share the returned redacted images
Encrypt the images with a customer-managed key, so the third party sees only ciphertext of the sensitive areas of each picture

stem: A security team wants to be told when a BigQuery table in any of 400 projects becomes more sensitive than before, for example because a new column now holds national ID numbers, and wants high-risk findings to appear next to other issues in its central security tooling. Which setup meets this?

choices.text: Create an organization-level discovery scan configuration with actions for Security Command Center and Pub/Sub on sensitivity changes
Use Data Access audit logs to find which columns are read, and treat frequently read columns as sensitive
Schedule inspection jobs on each table nightly, and write the findings to a spreadsheet for the team to review
Apply a de-identification template to every table, so all columns are treated as sensitive regardless of their real content

stem: A data governance lead is evaluating Sensitive Data Protection discovery for BigQuery and Cloud SQL. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Discovery requires each table to be exported to a dedicated Cloud Storage bucket before profiling
Profiling BigQuery data generates a table data profile, column data profiles and a project data profile
Discovery profiles only the data in the project in which the scan configuration was created
Discovery automatically masks the detected columns so that analysts see only asterisks
Discovery can send profile results to Security Command Center, and can notify via Pub/Sub when sensitivity changes

stem: A pipeline tokenizes customer IDs with Sensitive Data Protection using deterministic encryption and a transient key. A month later, a compliance team must re-identify some IDs from archived tokens, but the re-identification fails, and tokens created on different days do not match for the same customer. What should have been done?

choices.text: Use a key wrapped by Cloud KMS, keep it available to the re-identifying service, and use the same key for every run
Increase the likelihood threshold of the inspection, so that the tokenized values are recognised on re-identification
Switch to cryptographic hashing, because hashed tokens can be re-identified using the original key
Add a surrogate annotation to the tokens, because that restores the key used to create them

stem: A customer-service platform stores email addresses of very different lengths and containing any characters in a BigQuery column. Analysts must be able to join records for the same customer, and a privileged service must be able to reverse the tokens later. Which transformation fits best?

choices.text: Pseudonymization with format preserving encryption, using the numeric alphabet
Pseudonymization with cryptographic hashing, which is reversible with the original key
Pseudonymization with deterministic encryption using AES-SIV and a Cloud KMS wrapped key
Redaction of the email column, with a copy of the original values kept in a second dataset

stem: A marketing platform tokenizes email addresses so that the same person can be linked within a single campaign but must not be linkable across different campaigns by anyone holding the data. Which Sensitive Data Protection setting achieves this?

choices.text: Turn on a surrogate annotation using the campaign name, because that annotation changes the encrypted value itself
Use bucketing on the email column with one range per campaign
Use a different transient key per API request, so tokens never repeat across requests
Use a context tweak that references the campaign ID column when applying deterministic or format preserving encryption

stem: A team de-identifies free-text chat transcripts with deterministic encryption, replacing detected phone numbers with tokens. Later, a re-identification request on the transcripts returns the tokens unchanged, although the right key is used. What was missing at de-identification time?

choices.text: A larger set of infoTypes in the inspection, because additional detectors let the service reverse any token it finds
A masking character configuration, since masked tokens can be reversed by the key
A surrogate annotation on the tokens, which unstructured text needs to locate and reverse them
A bucketing range on the phone numbers, because ranges are needed to find them again

stem: A privacy engineer must choose transformations that an authorised pipeline can later reverse to restore original values. Which TWO Sensitive Data Protection transformations support re-identification? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Pseudonymization with cryptographic hashing (HMAC-SHA-256)
Pseudonymization with format preserving encryption (FPE-FFX)
Redaction of the detected value
Character masking of the value with an asterisk
Pseudonymization with deterministic encryption using AES-SIV

stem: A platform team stores API credentials in the environment variables of Cloud Run services across many projects. The security team wants to learn about secrets stored there without moving them into every team's own tooling. Which capability helps?

choices.text: Image redaction in Sensitive Data Protection, which scans the container environment variable text for any secrets inside
Cloud NAT logging, which records the secret values leaving the services over translated connections
Private Service Connect backends, which scan the traffic from the services for credential patterns
Sensitive Data Protection discovery, detecting secrets in Cloud Run environment variables and sending findings to Security Command Center

stem: An inspection of support tickets flags many order numbers like ORD-48213 as national ID numbers, creating noise, while internal employee codes in a custom format are never found. What should the security engineer change in the inspection configuration?

choices.text: Add a custom regex infoType for the employee code and an exclusion rule for the order-number pattern in the inspection ruleset
Lower the minimum likelihood to the lowest level, so more candidate matches are returned and the noise disappears
Run the scan as a discovery configuration, which ignores any strings that are not found in a built-in infoType
Switch to cryptographic hashing so that all numeric strings in the tickets are replaced by uniform tokens
